issue.close_reason:
Implemented in commit 74dd4de: alert dedup is now a stateful per-episode lifecycle instead of a cooldown timer. An episode is one continuous stretch during which a condition holds, keyed by alert type + scope. First cycle true -> create ONE bead and store its id in governor-state.json under open_alert_beads; while it stays true -> no new bead, refresh the existing one's notes at most once per cooldown_minutes; first cycle not true -> auto-close the bead with a reason and drop the entry. cooldown_minutes survives only as an anti-flap floor on OPENING a new episode after one resolves, so a flapping condition still cannot mint a bead per toggle. Bead volume is now bounded by distinct incidents rather than elapsed time -- the structural cause of the 226 sonnet_cutoff_risk / 160 cutoff_imminent bead pileup.

Touches: state (OpenAlertBead + open_alert_beads, serde default so existing state files load unchanged), alerts (AlertCondition scope + episode_key, fire_alert returns the bead id, new close_alert_bead/refresh_alert_bead/process_alert_episodes), config (close_command/update_command; create command now 'bf create --json --type human --title' so the id is parseable), governor (cycle 8 drives it; FP telemetry now records once per episode, measuring incidents not cooldown windows), status display (lists open episodes with bead ids).

alerts.auto_bead stays false -- the <5% FP-rate gate from docs-878a is untouched. What changed is that re-enabling it can no longer reproduce the spam, since the failure mode was structural.

Verified this pass: all 20 test targets pass, 0 failed (781 in the lib suite); the end-to-end test runs against the real bf 0.4.0 CLI and confirms one bead created, refreshed in place, then auto-closed; alerts.rs and state.rs are fmt-clean; no new clippy warnings.

issue.description: src/alerts.rs::should_fire()/process_alerts() dedup purely on a per-alert-type cooldown timer (default 60 minutes, alerts.cooldown_minutes in governor.yaml): while a condition remains true past the cooldown window, fire_alert() creates a brand-new bead via the configured command every time the cooldown elapses, rather than tracking one open bead per distinct condition episode. Historical bead data in this repo's own .beads workspace bears this out: bf list --json shows 226 closed beads titled starting with '[WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk' and 160 titled '[CRITICAL] cutoff_imminent' (out of 517 total issue_type=human alert beads created historically), almost certainly representing far fewer distinct real incidents than that count of beads. Redesign the alert lifecycle: on first firing of a given (alert_type, window) condition, create one bead and remember its bead id in governor-state.json (e.g. under alert_cooldown or a new open_alert_beads map); on subsequent cycles where the condition is still true, update/comment on the existing bead instead of creating a new one (or simply suppress, since the bead is already open and visible); when the condition clears, auto-close the bead. This is a natural extension of the auto_bead FP-rate gating work already done (see docs-878a, notes/bf-h7toj.md, and the alert_fp_telemetry struct in src/state.rs which already tracks true/false-positive outcomes per alert type) and should be done as part of re-enabling alerts.auto_bead so re-enablement doesn't reproduce the original spam problem. Umbrella: claudego-1ba35288. Child 4 of 5, depends on child 3 (claudego-de769d30).

The non-binding-window path in compute_composite_safe_workers (src/burn_rate.rs:816-822) is deliberately floor(), NOT duty_cycle_safe_workers: it only ever raises the target ABOVE the binding window's count, and its budget would be spent past the *binding* window's ceiling — that window has already said it can afford nothing. Lifting a fractional quotient to 1 there would cross that ceiling on a partial budget. The inconsistency with the duty-cycle path is intentional; pin the floor so nobody "fixes" it by lifting this quotient too.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- One test: a binding window whose safe count is 0, plus a non-binding window whose cross-window quotient is fractional (e.g. remaining_pct 0.9, pct_per_worker 1.0 = fleet 3.0 over 3 workers, binding_hours 1.0 → quotient 0.9), must yield None from compute_composite_safe_workers — the fractional quotient does NOT raise the target above the binding count of 0.
- No production code changes; report a failure against the umbrella (claudego-1ba35288).
- Scoped verification (immune to the unrelated failing bin test — see claudego-a541d6ce): `~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --lib fractional_quotient`.

NOTE (2026-09-08): an earlier attempt on the umbrella left an uncommitted test `compute_composite_safe_workers_fractional_quotient_not_lifted_above_binding` (verified passing) — check `git diff src/burn_rate.rs` before writing.

Scoped verification per claudego-a541d6ce: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --lib fractional_quotient → 1 passed (compute_composite_safe_workers_fractional_quotient_not_lifted_above_binding), 0 failed. issue.description:
## Task: Daemon Management — systemd and tmux Modes

Implement cgov start/stop/restart/enable/disable with dual-mode daemon management.

### What to Implement
- In `src/daemon.rs` (new module):
  - Mode detection: check for systemd user session availability
  - **Mode A: systemd user service** (Linux default):
    - `cgov enable`: install unit files, daemon-reload, enable + start both services
    - `cgov disable`: stop + disable both services
    - `cgov start`: start services (must be enabled first)
    - `cgov stop`: graceful stop (governor finishes current cycle)
    - `cgov restart`: stop + start
    - Unit files: claude-governor.service and claude-token-collector.service
  - **Mode B: tmux sessions** (fallback):
    - `cgov start`: `tmux new-session -d -s "claude-governor" "cgov _daemon"` (and token-collector)
    - `cgov stop`: send SIGTERM to tmux session processes
  - `_daemon` internal subcommand: the actual daemon entrypoint (used by both modes)
  - `_token-collector` internal subcommand: token collector entrypoint
  - Store chosen mode in governor.yaml as `daemon_mode: systemd|tmux`
  - `cgov logs --follow` works with both modes (tails log file directly)

### Files
- `src/daemon.rs` (new module)
- `systemd/claude-governor.service` (template)
- `systemd/claude-token-collector.service` (template)
- `src/main.rs` (add daemon subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: systemd detection logic
- Unit test: service file installation to correct path (~/.config/systemd/user/)
- Unit test: tmux fallback creates correct sessions
- Unit test: stop waits for current cycle completion

### Acceptance Criteria
- Auto-detects systemd vs tmux
- Services survive reboot when enabled via systemd
- tmux fallback works on systems without systemd
- Graceful stop ensures no mid-cycle interruption
- Logs accessible regardless of daemon mode

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7) — needs _daemon entrypoint
issue.title: P6: Daemon management — systemd and tmux modes

issue.description:
## Task: Prediction Accuracy Self-Calibration

Track prediction accuracy and auto-tune governor parameters based on historical performance.

### What to Implement
- New `src/calibrator.rs` module:
  - `score_prediction(window, predicted_pct, actual_pct) -> PredictionScore`:
    - `prediction_error = actual_final_pct - predicted_final_pct`
    - Negative = conservative, positive = aggressive
    - `correct`: predicted exhaustion matched actual
  - Append scored predictions to `~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl`
  - Hook into window reset events to trigger scoring
  - `CalibrationState`: predictions_scored, median_error per window, auto-tuned params
  - Auto-tuning rules (activated after >= 10 scored predictions per window):
    - Median error < -5 (conservative): increase burn_rate_alpha +0.02, widen hysteresis +0.5
    - Median error > +5 (aggressive): decrease alpha -0.02, tighten hysteresis -0.5
    - Stddev > 10 (unpredictable): lower target_utilization -0.02
  - Clamp ranges: alpha [0.05, 0.5], hysteresis [0, 3], target_util [0.70, 0.98]
  - Write calibration state to governor-state.json
  - Auto-tuning opt-in via `calibration.auto_calibrate: true` in config

### Files
- `src/calibrator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod calibrator`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: scoring with known prediction/actual pairs
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — conservative data increases alpha
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — aggressive data decreases alpha
- Unit test: clamp enforcement at boundaries
- Unit test: no tuning until 10 predictions scored
- Unit test: JSONL append format

### Acceptance Criteria
- Prediction accuracy tracked per window
- Auto-tuning adjusts parameters in correct direction
- Clamps prevent runaway parameter drift
- Opt-in via config (tracking always active, tuning optional)
- JSONL file serves as audit trail

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast to score
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — writes calibration state
issue.title: P7: Prediction accuracy self-calibration

issue.description:
git.ardenone.com has returned HTTP 503 'no available server' for all operations since ~2026-08-07T01:43Z, blocking every 'git push origin' from this and other repos on the host.

Root cause (verified twice, 07:20 and 07:45 UTC 2026-08-07): pod forgejo-gitea-769476465f-njdc5 in namespace 'forgejo' of cluster iad-ci (reachable via ~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig) is 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff, 55 restarts, pod age 7d12h. It aborts fatally on every start:

  modules/storage/minio.go:97 NewMinioStorage() [I] Creating Minio storage at armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000:iad-ci with base path forgejo/storage/attachments/
  routers/init.go:62 mustInit() [F] code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/storage.Init failed: permission denied

Forgejo 10.0.0+gitea-1.22.0 fails initialising its MinIO/S3 attachment storage. In gitea 1.22 that path is BucketExists/MakeBucket, and 'permission denied' is convertMinioErr's mapping of S3 AccessDenied. Traefik therefore has zero healthy endpoints behind the git.ardenone.com IngressRoute, which is why Cloudflare Tunnel returns 503 -- the tunnel and Traefik are fine, the backend is dead.

Supporting evidence:
- Config: forgejo-application.yml sets [storage] and [lfs] STORAGE_TYPE=minio, MINIO_ENDPOINT=armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000, MINIO_BUCKET=iad-ci. Credentials come from secret forgejo-backup-armor (keys auth-access-key / auth-secret-key).
- The credential is present and fresh: all 5 externalsecrets in ns forgejo report SecretSynced/True.
- ARMOR itself is UP and serving that same bucket: pod armor-69cdbb4d46-24d22 1/1 Running, thousands of status-200 requests including GETs under /iad-ci/forgejo/. So this is a bucket-level authz regression (HEAD bucket / MakeBucket on 'iad-ci' denied) rather than an ARMOR outage, while prefixed object GET/PUT for the same credential succeeds.
- Probably the same regression: CNPG backups in ns forgejo are also failing ('Backup failed' events for forgejo-postgres-daily-* and forgejo-postgres-test-manual).
- postgres-1, forgejo-init and forgejo-backup pods are all 1/1 Running; only the web/git app is down.

Fix belongs in the ardenone-cluster / declarative-config domain, NOT in claude-governor: restore the bucket-level S3 permission for the forgejo-backup-armor credential on bucket 'iad-ci' in the ARMOR object store, or reconfigure Forgejo's storage backend. Deliberately not done unilaterally from a claude-governor bead -- it is a production authz change in a separate system.

Impact while open: no repo on this host can push to origin. claude-governor specifically is 28 commits ahead of origin/main (local 50f1fc7, origin/main 7a06f2d); those commits were rescued to the GitHub mirror under bf-4najn, but other repos may not have a mirror and remain stranded.

Acceptance criteria:
- curl https://git.ardenone.com/ returns 200
- forgejo-gitea pod is 1/1 Running with 0 recent restarts
- 'git push origin main' from /home/coding/claude-governor advances origin/main to the local HEAD
- CNPG backups in ns forgejo succeed again

object store: orphans existing attachments/LFS under iad-ci/forgejo/, needs a

defect in place to recur at the next rotation. It converts a stale-config bug

issue.description:
## Problem

As of 2026-04-23, every single one of the 50 most recently closed beads in claude-governor is a `docs-*` bead that was auto-created from an alert (`sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline`) and closed with a commit of the form:

```
Document docs-jnvh as emergency_brake_activated false positive (98% util, -17.2h margin)
Document docs-q4sj as sonnet_cutoff_risk false positive (86% util, -16.2h margin)
Document docs-tggx as cutoff_imminent false positive (99% util, -16.2h margin)
```

**FP rate in the observed window: 50/50 = 100%.** This loop produces ~298 commits/7d — about 25% of total repo-wide commit volume — with zero engineering value.

## Fleet impact

- Workers spend ~25% of capacity round-tripping these alerts (alert fires → `docs-*` bead spawns → worker claims → "document as false positive" commit → close).
- When a worker dies mid-alert-handling, the `docs-*` bead becomes an in_progress zombie. 19 of the 53 total in_progress beads on 2026-04-22 were stuck claude-governor alerts with ages 50h–220h.
- Velocity metrics are inflated: real engineering work is ~127 commits/day vs. a reported ~169. The 500 commits/day target is 25% of the way there, not 34%.

## Suspected root cause

The alert bodies report utilization `81%–99%` alongside margins of `-15.2h` to `-23.2h` (negative). A negative margin at sub-100% util is self-contradictory — either the margin math is wrong or the thresholds are inverted. Whichever it is, the predicate that fires these alerts is broken across every alert type uniformly, not just one.

Starting points for investigation:
- Burn-rate / margin calculation that feeds `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`.
- The `safe_worker_count` fallback logic (separately tracked in recent `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4` beads — all flagged as bugs, none yet fixed).

## Fix in two parts

**(1) Correct the alert predicates** so the FP rate drops below 5% measured across any 100-bead window.

**(2) Interim mitigation: gate the alert→bead pipeline.** Until (1) lands, stop auto-creating beads for these alert classes. Keep the alert logs for diagnosis; don't burn fleet cycles documenting false positives. Concrete options:
  - Feature flag `governor.alerts.auto_bead = false` (fastest).
  - Require N consecutive cycles in alert state before spawning a bead (smooths out momentary spikes).
  - Suppress spawning when margin and utilization are inconsistent (e.g. negative margin at util < 100%).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FP rate for `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline` measured at <5% over a 100-bead rolling window.
- [ ] Beads are no longer auto-spawned for these alert classes until the FP rate target is met (interim mitigation in place within this bead).
- [ ] Telemetry/dashboard exposes alert FP rate so regressions are visible.
- [ ] New test: negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util alert is suppressed at source (consistency check).
- [ ] Existing zombie `docs-*` beads (ages >6h) are closed out as part of landing this fix.

## Related

- `needle-mv9t` (2026-04-22): cross-workspace mend gap — would clean up zombies produced by this loop, but doesn't address the root cause.
- `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4`: previously-identified governor bugs that likely share upstream causes.
issue.title: Alert thresholding produces 100% false positives; stop auto-creating beads for unvalidated alerts

issue.description:
## Task: Cache Efficiency Monitoring

Track per-worker and per-workspace cache hit ratios to identify inefficient consumption.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs` (extend):
  - Compute `cache_eff` per instance interval: `cache_read_tokens / (cache_read_tokens + input_tokens)`
  - When both are zero: cache_eff = null (undefined, excluded from aggregation)
  - Add `cache_eff` field to `i` records
  - Add `fleet_cache_eff` (mean) and `cache_eff_p25` (25th percentile) to `f` records
- In `src/db.rs` (extend):
  - `workspace_cache_eff` view: per-session average, min, sample count over last 24h
- In `src/alerts.rs` (extend):
  - Cache efficiency warning: when worker drops below `cache_efficiency.warn_threshold` (default 0.60)
    for `consecutive_intervals` (default 3) consecutive intervals
  - Log: `[governor] CACHE: {session} efficiency {eff} (fleet avg {fleet_avg})`
- In `src/cli.rs` (extend cgov status):
  - Add cache efficiency to status output: `Burn: $2.15/hr (p75) · Cache: 84% (fleet avg)`

### Files
- `src/collector.rs` (extend i and f record generation)
- `src/db.rs` (extend with view)
- `src/alerts.rs` (extend with cache alert)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: cache_eff computation with known token counts
- Unit test: null cache_eff when both zero
- Unit test: fleet_cache_eff aggregation
- Unit test: warning triggers after 3 consecutive low-efficiency intervals
- Unit test: warning does NOT trigger for transient dips (1-2 intervals)
- Unit test: workspace_cache_eff view returns correct aggregation

### Acceptance Criteria
- Per-instance cache efficiency tracked and stored
- Fleet-level aggregation in f records
- Sustained low efficiency generates warning
- Status display includes cache efficiency metric
- Null handling prevents division by zero

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b i/f record writer (docs-lfz) — extends record format
- Depends on: P5 alert conditions (docs-e5l) — adds new alert type
issue.title: P7: Cache efficiency monitoring

issue.close_reason: Row selection, guards, and apportionment all use the delta-measurement span [prev_snap.taken_at, now] as of ced3dc1; span-boundary and in-span apportionment tests added; 766 tests pass. Commit is local only -- remote push blocked by a 503 from git.ardenone.com.
issue.description:
At the annotation call site (src/governor.rs ~line 5570-5615) the time interval used to select rows does not match the interval the percentage delta was measured over.

Rows are selected by:  t0 = state.last_fleet_aggregate.t0, t1 = state.last_fleet_aggregate.t1  (the COLLECTOR's aggregation window)
Delta is computed from: old_pct = prev_snap (captured at prev_usage_snapshot.taken_at) vs new_pct = state.usage.* (captured at 'now') - the API POLL interval

These two intervals are produced by different clocks/cadences and generally do not coincide. The result is that a delta measured over the poll interval is apportioned onto collector rows from a different span, so p5h/p7d/p7ds values are attributed to the wrong interval - and the <2min elapsed guard is evaluated against the collector window rather than the span the delta actually covers.

Fix: make the row-selection interval and the delta-measurement interval the same span. Prefer selecting the i/f rows whose [t0,t1] falls within [prev_snap.taken_at, now], or otherwise justify and document the mapping in a comment.

Depends on the worker-count fix so both call-site inputs are corrected together.

Acceptance criteria:
- Row-selection interval and delta-measurement interval refer to the same span, or the mapping between them is explicitly documented and justified at the call site
- The elapsed-time guard is evaluated against the span the delta actually covers
- Unit test: rows outside the delta-measurement span are not annotated
- Unit test: rows inside the span receive the apportioned delta
- cargo test passes
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-3p0tb]
Implemented in commit ced3dc1 (src/db.rs + src/governor.rs). Annotation call site now uses [prev_snap.taken_at, now] -- the same span the delta is measured over -- for row selection, the guard chain, and annotate_window_pct_deltas. Collector rows are claimed by t1 so contiguous spans partition rows without double-annotation or boundary loss; rationale documented in a comment at the call site. Range queries switched to julianday() because to_rfc3339() emits variable fractional digits. Tests: annotate_window_pct_deltas_ignores_rows_outside_the_delta_span, ..._apportions_across_every_pass_in_the_span, ..._measures_elapsed_over_the_span, and call-site regression test_annotation_follows_the_delta_span_not_the_collector_window. Full suite: 766 passed, 0 failed. NOT PUSHED: git.ardenone.com returns 503 'no available server' on push; commit is local on main (ahead 15). Needs a push once the remote is back.

issue.description:
get_multiplier_at() and effective_hours_remaining() apply the promotion multiplier globally to all windows, but the Promotion struct has an applies_to field that is never checked. The March 2026 promotion only applies to the five_hour window — the seven_day and seven_day_sonnet windows should always get 1.0x.

Fix: add a window parameter to get_multiplier_at() and effective_hours_remaining() (or create per-window variants). The governor should call these per-window when computing capacity_forecast, passing the window name so only the applies_to windows get the boost.

Current state: applies_to is stored in the JSON but ignored. State stores a single effective_hours_remaining instead of per-window values.
issue.title: Promotion multiplier ignores applies_to — applied globally instead of per-window

issue.description:
Found 2026-09-08 while splitting claudego-1ba35288: full `cargo test` fails on this repo — 796 lib tests pass, but the --bin cgov target fails tests::test_individual_half_does_not_fall_back_to_combined_unit (src/main.rs:2835):

  panicked at src/main.rs:2843:9: no observe unit exists here: ["claude-governor.service"]

Every worker whose acceptance says "cargo test passes" trips over this; it is very plausibly why claudego-1ba35288 failed 3 times in a row.

ROOT CAUSE: resolve_installed_service_names (src/main.rs:1492-1498) falls back to COMBINED_SERVICE for ANY service with non-empty governor_units — which includes the individual halves ("observe" -> [OBSERVE_SERVICE], "act" -> [ACT_SERVICE]), not just the "governor" compatibility alias. The test at src/main.rs:2835 pins the intended contract: restarting `observe` on a combined-unit host must resolve to nothing and fail loudly, because the combined unit also runs the act half — restarting it under the observe name would restart a daemon it does not name (and vice versa for `act`).

The regression came in with commit 6e60abe (the test was added, the contract was left unmet). Not covered by any open bead at filing time (checked 2026-09-08; claudego-6960e911 is the adjacent restart-targets symptom, not this resolver contract).

FIX DIRECTION: apply the combined fallback only where the combined unit genuinely stands in for the whole target — the "governor" alias (and the "all"/catch-all), never an individual half. Re-check the neighbouring tests at src/main.rs:2791-2870 ("all", "governor", half-installed, target loop) so the contract stays consistent; if any of them pins the fallback for a half, that assertion is the wrong one — split it out rather than weaken it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- tests::test_individual_half_does_not_fall_back_to_combined_unit passes unmodified.
- Full `cargo test` passes (lib 796+, bin and integration targets all green).
- cgov restart observe / act on a host with only claude-governor.service installed errors naming the combined unit, instead of restarting it.
- The "governor" alias keeps its legitimate mapping to the combined unit when the split units are absent.

Implement worker attribution:
- Resolve each collected Claude Code session to a live NEEDLE worker -- map the
  transcript JSONL path or the session's cwd to a running worker via
  ~/.needle/state/heartbeats or needle's worker registry -- OR have NEEDLE stamp
  its worker identifier into the dispatched environment so the claude-print child
  session carries it and the collector can read it.
- Write the resolved identifier into a NEW field on the record; leave sess
  untouched so existing history stays parseable.

- Records from fleet-dispatched sessions carry the worker identifier; operator /
  interactive sessions leave it absent (null).
- Values in the new field match the agent session_pattern globs in governor.yaml.
- Old history lines without the field still parse (serde default).
- Unit test for the mapping; no change to existing field shapes.

Found 2026-09-13 by claudego-ca4590e5 (full-suite acceptance gate for umbrella claudego-a541d6ce). Filed from that bead per its out-of-scope-failure protocol; NOT fixed there.

FAILURE (deterministic — 3/3 isolated reruns + full-suite run, all identical):
tests/promotion_validation_live_path_test.rs::the_api_delta_ema_is_unaffected_by_annotation_data
  panicked at tests/promotion_validation_live_path_test.rs:600:5:
  five_hour pct/hr EMA: bare 0 vs annotated 0 diverged beyond span jitter
assert_ema_close computes ((bare - annotated) / annotated).abs() < 0.01 — with both EMAs pinned to 0 this is 0/0 = NaN, and NaN < 0.01 is false. The panic message's '0 vs 0' is the tell: it is not a divergence, it is the tolerance division NaN-ing on two zeros. seven_day and weekly_scoped EMAs and all usd/pct EMAs still pass their assertions.

ATTRIBUTION (bisected by clean-checkout runs, clones removed after each):
- 29da65a (pre-chain base, parent of ac3123e): PASSES — 4/4 in the target.
- de7e840 'fix(governor): guard zero-worker burn so idle account spend is not fleet burn (claudego-8c7890ab)': FAILS — same panic.
- HEAD a807993 + current dirty tree: FAILS (the dirty hunks are all inside mod tests blocks, which integration tests do not compile — the integration run sees HEAD's production code).
Only two commits in 29da65a..HEAD touch src/: de7e840 (production) and a807993 (test-only). de7e840 is the introducing commit.

MECHANISM: the test harness runs the observe cycle with zero workers running. de7e840 pins the fleet rate to 0 when current_workers == 0 (the intended guard — the in-flight claudego-6f45312e tests assert exactly that: '0 workers must pin the fleet rate to 0' across all three windows). The five_hour pct/hr EMA the test reads is therefore 0 in both the bare and annotated runs, and the test's own premise — 'the EMA is only meaningful if it actually moved' — no longer holds in the zero-worker regime. The test's invariant is stale relative to the new contract; it is NOT evidence that de7e840 is wrong.

FIX DIRECTION (for whoever takes this): do NOT revert de7e840's guard. Rework the test instead — either (a) seed the harness so the cycle runs with >= 1 worker attributed, restoring a nonzero EMA to compare, or (b) assert the new contract directly: with 0 workers the EMA/rate is pinned to 0 in BOTH runs and annotation still perturbs nothing (compare pinned zeros with assert_eq, and move the jitter comparison to a regime with a nonzero EMA). Guard the helper against the NaN case either way (assert both nonzero before dividing, so a future pin degrades into a clear message, not NaN).

IMPACT: 'cargo test green' acceptance criteria across the fleet's beads cannot pass on this repo until this lands — every worker running the full suite hits it (claudego-ca4590e5 attempt 1 hit it 2026-09-12, before the attribution existed).

EVIDENCE LOGS: test-outputs/ (gitignored, this machine): ca4590e5-full-run.log (full suite, per-target), ca4590e5-base-commit-run.log (base pass), ca4590e5-bisect-de7e840.log (first-fail). Full failure text is inlined above; logs are convenience copies, the bead is canonical.

issue.description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- List all configuration files that control bead visibility in Pluck
- Map each configuration file to its scope (global, workspace, local)
- Document the configuration precedence/order
- Identify any configuration files that may be overriding expected settings

## Purpose

Understand where and how bead visibility is configured, so we can trace why beads might be hidden.

## Dependencies

- Requires: Documentation of Pluck configuration settings (from child bead 1)
issue.notes:
Investigation complete (2026-08-20; verified against current NEEDLE source and live files).

Active/current controls:
1. GLOBAL: /home/coding/.config/needle/config.yaml. ConfigLoader hardcodes this path. Current values: workspace.default=/home/coding/aide-de-camp (high-risk wrong home Pluck store for claude-governor when --workspace is omitted); workspace.home=/home/coding/.needle (NEEDLE state only, not bead DB); strands.pluck.exclude_labels=[deferred,human,blocked,starvation-alert] (exact label exclusions); strands.pluck.split_after_failures=3 (can defer/split processing but is not a candidate filter); strands.pluck.persistent_starvation_records=false (diagnostics only); strands.explore.enabled=true, workspaces=[], workspace_root=/home/coding/ (auto-discovers all .beads workspaces, so Explore can roam outside the home workspace). The four-label non-empty list replaces, rather than merges with, the Pluck source fallback.
2. WORKSPACE: /home/coding/claude-governor/.needle.yaml. Current value bead_cli.backend=bead-rs. It selects the backend/store implementation and therefore indirectly affects ready semantics, but contains no Pluck label/status filter. Current WorkspaceOverrides only applies agent, weave/pulse/unravel, prompt, verification/gates, workspace.labels, and bead_cli; strands.pluck in this file is not a supported workspace override.
3. WORKSPACE: /home/coding/claude-governor/.beads/config.json. Active bead-rs identity metadata (prefix=claudego, UUID, version); it identifies the store but defines no Pluck visibility filters. The live store is /home/coding/claude-governor/.beads/beads.db; ready-frontier state (open, unassigned, not manually blocked, no unresolved blocking dependency) is data/runtime filtering, not config.
4. GLOBAL orchestration: /home/coding/.config/claude-governor/governor.yaml. Its active launch_cmd contains needle run ... --workspace {workspace}; cgov substitutes its own current working directory, so this CLI workspace can override NEEDLE workspace.default. The repo template config/governor.yaml is only the development/install fallback; it is not loaded when the installed XDG config exists.
5. LOCAL per-worker systemd: /home/coding/.config/needle/workers/*.env plus /home/coding/.config/systemd/user/needle-worker@.service. NEEDLE_WS in each env and the unit's explicit needle run with the NEEDLE_WS value select the home store for that worker. These are local machine/worker scope, not Pluck label config. The current luna-cgov process was launched with --workspace /home/coding/claude-governor.

Precedence:
NEEDLE ConfigLoader order is built-in defaults -> /home/coding/.config/needle/config.yaml -> target workspace .needle.yaml (limited supported fields) -> recognized NEEDLE_* env overrides -> CLI overrides (documented in NEEDLE/src/config/mod.rs and implemented by load_resolved). Config is loaded once at boot. For workspace selection, NEEDLE_WORKSPACE__DEFAULT can override the global path and --workspace is higher; cgov/systemd launch commands inject --workspace outside the YAML hierarchy. Current source has no recognized env or CLI override for strands.pluck.exclude_labels, so its effective sources are the global value or the hardcoded fallback when the global list is empty. Runtime ready-frontier/data and Pluck defensive status/assignee/label checks remain downstream gates.

Potential overrides/false leads:
- /home/coding/.needle/config.yaml is a stale legacy duplicate that says workspace.default=/home/coding/claude-governor, but current ConfigLoader does not read it; it can create false confidence.
- /home/coding/.config/needle/explore-excluded exists, but current NEEDLE source has no reader for this path; it is inert for the current Explore implementation (and it does not list claude-governor anyway). Do not treat it as an active exclusion override.
- /home/coding/claude-governor/.beads/config.yaml is absent; legacy bf/br config files elsewhere are not the active bead-rs configuration for this workspace.
- Any explicit --workspace in a launch command, systemd EnvironmentFile, or manually exported recognized NEEDLE_WORKSPACE__DEFAULT can supersede the global default. Check the resolved worker command/environment before blaming labels.
- The existing docs/research/bead-visibility-configuration.md and earlier plan text contain historical bf/br claims; the consolidated plan also says the current TLS string causes a config-load failure, but needle config --dump --show-source succeeds now. Treat those claims as stale unless reverified.

No repository source/documentation files were changed; findings are recorded here on the bead.
issue.title: Identify bead visibility configuration files

issue.notes:
Residual gap found while landing claudego-f5018d81 (pool window affinity), 2026-09-19. Not a regression — it is the price of the fix for a different, worse bug, and it is inert on codinghome today.

WHAT: distribute_workers_by_cost_priority applies each pool's window-affinity ceiling, then re-homes the freed slots to pools with headroom, and returns whatever cannot be re-homed to the pool it came from — bounded by that pool's CURRENT worker count. The bounding rule is deliberate: the cap must not shed a pool faster than the aggregate decision authorized shedding the fleet, because target_total already carries the hysteresis band and max_scale_down_per_cycle. Clamping the allocation outright instead (the shape the uncommitted working tree had) made a NoChange cycle signal a worker and an authorized shed of 2 signal 3 — see graceful_idle_scaling_test::hysteresis_hold_touches_no_worker_regression and ::scale_down_honors_per_cycle_cap_regression, both of which failed on the pre-fix code.

THE GAP: when the aggregate holds (target_total == current_total) and there is no other pool with headroom to absorb the freed slots, a pool sitting above its OWN window ceiling is given its workers back and sheds nothing that cycle. Worked example: pool A [five_hour, seven_day] at max 8 and running 8, pool B declaring all three windows running 3, weekly_scoped safe_worker_count 0, seven_day safe 5. The affinity gate correctly stops weekly_scoped binding the aggregate, the aggregate holds, A has no headroom, and B keeps its 3 workers despite weekly_scoped saying 0.

WHY IT IS INERT TODAY: needle-sonnet is the only configured pool (polish-opus was removed 2026-09-18), so there is no second pool to create the contention, and a single pool's ceiling only matters on the growth path, which IS bounded absolutely. The 98% emergency brake is not affinity-gated and still zeroes every pool including on weekly_scoped.

FIX DIRECTION (not decided): the shed belongs at the aggregate level, not in the distribution — compute_target_workers should notice that some pool is above its own window ceiling and authorize a shed for it, so the move passes through max_scale_down_per_cycle like every other shed instead of being smuggled through the distribution pass. Do NOT fix it by removing the give-back; that reintroduces the two regression failures above. Add a second declared pool to the test matrix when this is worked.
=== RESOLUTION (2026-09-20, chain tail claudego-cf553456) ===

IMPLEMENTING FIX: commit ac82e32 ("fix(governor): authorize the window-affinity shed at the aggregate", origin/main HEAD) — exactly the fix direction recorded above, not the clamping shape the regressions rejected. affinity_shed_target (src/governor.rs:4915) computes supported/excess across pools from the shared pool_affinity_ceiling (src/governor.rs:4875); run_act_cycle lowers computed_target when Some(bound) < computed_target (src/governor.rs:7226-7240), so the shed paces through hysteresis + max_scale_down_per_cycle like every other down-move. The distribution give-back is untouched. The worked example above now converges: pool B above its own weekly_scoped 0 ceiling sheds on a hold cycle, paced 2 then 1 at cap 2, pool A untouched.

SPLIT CHAIN (auto-split umbrella, three children):
- claudego-4ec46cc6 (audit sibling, CLOSED) — audit of ac82e32 against this bead's fix direction. VERDICT: PASS on all 4 points, no gaps. [1] affinity_shed_target exists and is wired at the aggregate, after compute_target_workers and before resolve_manual_override / apply_underutilization_sprint, and only ever lowers (never gates a hold, growth, or cold start). [2] pool_affinity_ceiling is the single source of the per-pool bound — all three consumers (distribution clamp, re-home bound, aggregate shed) call it; the commit's only structural deletion is the former inline closure, no site computes the bound independently. [3] the give-back in distribute_workers_by_cost_priority is NOT removed: give-back block intact and bounded by what the pool is already running; both give-back regression tests (hysteresis_hold_touches_no_worker_regression, scale_down_honors_per_cycle_cap_regression) still exist and pass. issue.description:
~/.needle/state/token-history.jsonl and its SQLite mirror token-history.db grow without bound.

Evidence, 2026-09-23: token-history.jsonl is 688 MB (231,338 lines, first record 2026-03-21, one per 5-minute interval); token-history.db is 770 MB (tables `i` 111,198 rows, `f` 120,114 rows, `w` 0 rows). src/db.rs line 1 documents the db as "SQLite mirror of token-history.jsonl for fast queries", so it is a derived cache of the jsonl. A search of src/db.rs, src/governor.rs and src/burn_rate.rs finds no retention, prune, vacuum or rotation code for either file. Both files were still being written at 18:26 on 2026-09-23. Together they are 1.5 GB and rising.

Decisions (locked):
1. Retention window = the larger of 90 days and the longest lookback any reader in src actually uses. Measure that lookback first (burn-rate, governor, doctor, and the dow/hr_et seasonal fields) and record it here; do not guess.
2. The working token-history.jsonl keeps only the window. Older records move to monthly compressed archives token-history-YYYY-MM.jsonl.gz in the same directory (kept, ~10x smaller), never deleted.
3. The db mirror deletes rows older than the window and runs an incremental vacuum; it must remain rebuildable from the jsonl.
4. The path ~/.needle/state/token-history.jsonl stays where it is (src/doctor.rs reads it at ~line 203).

Acceptance criteria:
1. The measured max reader lookback is recorded on this bead with the code locations.
2. A test with a synthetic 300-day history leaves the working jsonl and db holding only the window and the archives holding the rest, with total record count preserved (jsonl + archives == input).
3. `doctor` still finds and validates token-history.jsonl after rotation.
4. Rotation is idempotent (running twice changes nothing) and safe against a concurrent append.
issue.title: token-history.jsonl and its SQLite mirror grow without bound (688 MB + 770 MB since 2026-03-21)

## Task: Promotion Boundary Pre-Scaling

Anticipate multiplier transitions and begin scaling down before the boundary hits.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` (extend):
  - `next_transition(promotions) -> Option<(DateTime, f64, f64)>`:
    - Return next upcoming multiplier change (time, old_multiplier, new_multiplier)
    - E.g., (2026-03-19T08:00:00 ET, 2.0, 1.0) when off-peak ends
  - Pre-scale logic in `src/governor.rs`:
    - If transition within `pre_scale_minutes` (default 30 from config):
      - Compute post-transition target workers using new multiplier
      - If post-transition target < current workers: begin scaling down
      - Scale down at most 1 worker per cycle (gradual)
      - `effective_target = max(post_target, current_workers - 1)`
  - Conservative-only: pre-scale DOWN before losing bonus, never pre-scale UP
  - Logging: `[governor] PRE-SCALE: off-peak→peak in {min}min — scaling {from}→{to} (post-transition safe: {safe})`

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (extend with next_transition)
- `src/governor.rs` (extend with pre-scale check)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: next_transition at 07:35 ET during promo returns (08:00, 2.0, 1.0)
- Unit test: next_transition at 13:35 ET during promo returns (14:00, 1.0, 2.0)
- Unit test: pre-scale triggers 30 min before transition
- Unit test: pre-scale does NOT trigger 31 min before transition
- Unit test: pre-scale only scales down, never up
- Unit test: gradual scale-down (max 1 worker per cycle)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly identifies next multiplier transition
- Pre-scales only when losing capacity bonus (conservative-only)
- Gradual scale-down prevents sudden worker drops
- Configurable look-ahead window
- Clear logging of pre-scale decisions

### Dependencies

- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz)

issue.description:
CLAUDE.md documents that `needle test-agent claude-print-opus` is not sufficient proof (resolves agent_cli through PATH while dispatch runs invoke_template, so a missing binary still reports READY) and prescribes a manual check: run the installed template's invoke_template verbatim and require exit 0. It also documents two historically severe failure classes the adapters must stay immune to: inherited IDE env (CLAUDECODE/VSCODE_*, 46% of dispatches) and inherited API-routing env (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN/MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL — exit 124). Today only the installer's --version check is automated. Extend deploy/install-claude-print-adapters.sh and the claude_print check in `cgov doctor` to: (a) execute each installed template's invoke_template with a trivial prompt and require exit 0, and (b) verify the installed templates scrub the rule-3 and rule-5 variable sets (static check for the unset lines at minimum), so a regression of either class is caught before dispatch churn beads into stuck in_progress.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Automated the two authoritative adapter checks CLAUDE.md prescribed by hand, in both verification surfaces. Commit 7dbdd8f, pushed to Forgejo origin.

What shipped (src/adapter_verify.rs + doctor.rs + main.rs + install-claude-print-adapters.sh + CLAUDE.md note):
- Static env-scrub check: parses each installed template's invoke_template, requires every rule-3 (IDE: CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT/VSCODE_*) and rule-5 (API-routing: ANTHROPIC_*/CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL) variable inside an unset segment; names the missing vars and their failure class.
- Live invoke_template probe: renders the installed template verbatim ({workspace}={XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/claude-print-adapter-verify, {model} from the adapter, trivial single-word prompt), runs it under bash with a HARD-CAPPED timeout (min(adapter timeout_secs, 240s)) and requires exit 0 WITH output (silent-empty-output was the exit-127 incident's signature). The probe poisons all 20 rule-3/rule-5 vars in the child env (CLAUDECODE=1, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9, dummy model/auth), so a dropped unset fails deterministically instead of silently passing on a clean parent shell - it simulates the worst-case interactive/proxy-routed dispatcher.
- cgov doctor: new claude_print_adapters check, live by default, --skip-live flag added; warn (not fail) when no adapters are installed.
- Installer: same two checks after --version (--skip-live to opt out); aborts install on scrub regression or probe failure.

Verified live on this box: installer full run - both adapters scrub-clean, invoke_template exit 0 (fable 5.8s, opus 3.8s via doctor; 203KB/183KB stream-json via installer). cgov doctor --json includes the check. Negative tests: bash scrub detector flags a rule-5-regressed template (17 missing: 8 IDE + 9 API) and partially-unset rule 3; Rust stub tests cover nonzero exit, timeout, silent-empty, and poison-leak paths. 12 adapter_verify + 26 doctor tests pass; committed templates now carry a regression guard (committed_adapter_templates_scrub_both_variable_sets).

Notes for the record: (1) the test suite caught two real bugs in my own first draft - ${VAR} looks exactly like a {word} placeholder to a naive scanner (fixed with a $-lookbehind), and awk split() makes a leading separator an empty w[1], which hid every unset in the bash check (fixed with a sub() trim). (2) Pre-existing failure attribution: 17 burn_rate::tests failures in the shared tree belong to the concurrent scaling work (9f0f520 lineage), not this change - all doctor/adapter tests are green. (3) Full doctor run reports 1 pre-existing failure (prediction_accuracy median error 15.0%), unrelated to adapters.

ARMOR (git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ARMOR) is a bespoke single-bucket S3 gateway whose only authz is Credential.ACLs (config.go:20-30,184-201) checked by CheckACL (auth.go:293-317), called ONLY from server.go:715/904 on object paths. The iad-ci deployment (declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-deployment.yaml + armor-configmap.yaml) sets only ARMOR_AUTH_ACCESS_KEY/_SECRET_KEY, so exactly one credential exists with ACLs: nil = full access to bucket iad-ci. forgejo-backup-armor reads the SAME OpenBao properties (rs-manager/iad-ci/armor AUTH_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET) so it IS that credential. ARMOR has no s3:ListBucket/CreateBucket/GetObject action model at all; HeadBucket/CreateBucket are not ACL-gated. Regression commit: NO -- nearest commits to 2026-08-07T01:43Z (11a227ad, 9868516b) are unrelated, armor dir untouched since 2026-08-06 08:47. Real cause is the 2026-08-02 rotation (379bad72/e29db26d/175cc4d4) where forgejo-postgres was restarted but forgejo-gitea was not, leaving a stale app.ini -- matching bf-1tkap. CNPG failures: NO, not shared -- forgejo-postgres has current creds and fails on ARMOR multipart InvalidPartSize/ADR-005 (c8aefe75, d89f8e32, ARMOR fc6c1a86, notes/bf-1zh.md). No changes applied.
issue.description:
Read-only research in the ardenone-cluster / declarative-config domain. Depends on bf-1tkap having identified the exact denied operation.

Find where the S3/IAM policy for the ARMOR object store is declared: which repo, which path, which resource kind (MinIO policy CR, ARMOR-native policy config, ExternalSecret-fed policy doc, or hand-applied). Identify the policy statement(s) that currently attach to the forgejo-backup-armor credential and show why they permit s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::iad-ci/forgejo/* but deny the bucket-level action from bf-1tkap (typically a missing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::iad-ci, and/or missing s3:CreateBucket).

Also determine whether this changed recently: check git history of that policy file and the ARMOR deployment for a commit near 2026-08-07T01:43Z that would explain the regression, and whether the same missing grant explains the failing CNPG backups (forgejo-postgres-daily-*, forgejo-postgres-test-manual) in ns forgejo.

Acceptance criteria:
- Exact file path(s) + repo named for the policy source of truth.
- The current effective policy for the forgejo-backup-armor credential quoted verbatim.
- The specific missing action(s)/resource(s) named.
- A yes/no answer, with evidence, on whether a recent commit caused the regression and whether CNPG backup failures share the cause.

issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-385rj]
FINDING: There is NO bucket-policy source of truth, and NO missing grant. The task premise
(an IAM-style policy permitting s3:GetObject/PutObject on iad-ci/forgejo/* while denying a
bucket-level action) cannot be expressed in this system. This corroborates bf-1tkap, which
already DISPROVED the object-vs-bucket asymmetry.

== 1. Policy source of truth (exact paths + repos) ==
ARMOR is a bespoke single-bucket S3 gateway, not MinIO. Authorization is env-var-driven
credential config with an OPTIONAL, UNUSED ACL feature. Not a MinIO policy CR, not an
ExternalSecret-fed policy doc, not hand-applied.

Repo https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ARMOR.git (local /home/coding/ARMOR):
  internal/config/config.go:20-30    ACLEntry{Bucket,Prefix}; Credential{AccessKey,SecretKey,ACLs}
  internal/config/config.go:184-201  default credential registered with ACLs: nil
  internal/config/config.go:417-464  loadNamedCredentials, optional ARMOR_AUTH_<NAME>_ACL
  internal/server/auth.go:293-317    CheckACL - the ONLY authorization function
  internal/server/server.go:715,904  the ONLY two CheckACL call sites (object paths only)

Repo https://github.com/jedarden/declarative-config.git (local /home/coding/declarative-config):
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-deployment.yaml     container env, lines ~25-95
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-configmap.yaml      ARMOR_BUCKET: "iad-ci", ARMOR_PREFIX: ""
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-externalsecret.yaml OpenBao rs-manager/iad-ci/armor
  k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/forgejo-backup-externalsecret.yaml  the consumer

== 2. Current effective policy for forgejo-backup-armor, verbatim ==
forgejo-backup-externalsecret.yaml pulls AUTH_ACCESS_KEY / AUTH_SECRET_KEY from OpenBao
rs-manager/iad-ci/armor -- the SAME two properties armor-secrets feeds into ARMOR's own
ARMOR_AUTH_ACCESS_KEY / ARMOR_AUTH_SECRET_KEY. So forgejo-backup-armor IS ARMOR's default
credential. Its effective policy is, verbatim (config.go:193-199):

	// Initialize credentials map with default credential
	cfg.Credentials = make(map[string]*Credential)
	cfg.Credentials[cfg.AuthAccessKey] = &Credential{
		AccessKey: cfg.AuthAccessKey,
		SecretKey: cfg.AuthSecretKey,
		ACLs:      nil, // nil means full access to configured bucket
	}

and enforcement, verbatim (auth.go:293-298):

	// CheckACL verifies that the credential is allowed to access the given bucket and key.
	// If the credential has no ACLs (nil), it has full access.
	func CheckACL(cred *config.Credential, bucket, key string) error {
		// No ACLs means full access
		if len(cred.ACLs) == 0 {
			return nil
		}

The iad-ci deployment env sets NO ARMOR_AUTH_<NAME>_ACCESS_KEY, so loadNamedCredentials
finds zero names; cfg.Credentials has exactly one entry, ACLs nil => unconditional full access.

== 3. Missing action(s)/resource(s): NONE ==
ARMOR has no action-level authorization. CheckACL takes only (bucket, key) -- there is no
concept of s3:ListBucket / s3:CreateBucket / s3:GetObject as distinct grants. HeadBucket and
CreateBucket are not ACL-gated at all (CheckACL is called only from server.go:715 and :904,
both object paths). Nothing can be added to a policy because no policy object exists.
The 403 was AUTHENTICATION (SigV4 signature computed over a rotated secret), not authorization
-- exactly as bf-1tkap concluded: the stale key failed EVERY op including GetObject, and the
current key succeeded at HeadBucket/GetObject/PutObject.

== 4. Did a recent commit cause the regression? NO ==
Nearest declarative-config commits to 2026-08-07T01:43Z (= 2026-08-06 21:43 -0400):
  11a227ad 21:40:47 chore(data-stack): take down native-db-writer
  9868516b 21:47:52 feat(polaris): add a read-only data profiler
Neither touches ARMOR auth, forgejo credentials, or any policy.
k8s/iad-ci/armor/ was last touched ~13h earlier and not on credentials:
  68a17a9a 2026-08-06 08:47 fix(iad-ci/armor): disable dead ServiceMonitor/PrometheusRule
  c547d39c 2026-08-06 08:38 fix(iad-ci/armor): mount emptyDir at /tmp
The real causal event is older -- the 2026-08-02 credential rotation:
  379bad72 19:15 chore(iad-ci): force-sync ARMOR auth credential ExternalSecrets
  e29db26d 19:25 chore(iad-ci): restart armor to pick up rotated auth credentials
  175cc4d4 19:27 chore(iad-ci): restart forgejo-postgres to pick up rotated ARMOR backup creds
forgejo-postgres WAS restarted; forgejo-gitea was NOT. The gitea pod dates from ~2026-07-26
(64aa8af4 move to compute1-8, af7a6225 raise memory), matching bf-1tkap's app.ini mtime
2026-07-25. init-app-ini runs only at pod start, so gitea kept the pre-rotation key. The
breakage was LATENT from 2026-08-02 and surfaced whenever gitea next ran storage.Init.

== 5. Do the CNPG backup failures share the cause? NO ==
k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/cnpg-cluster.yaml:60-70 uses the same forgejo-backup-armor secret, but
forgejo-postgres was restarted for the rotation (175cc4d4), so it holds CURRENT credentials.
Its documented failure is ARMOR multipart block-alignment InvalidPartSize (ADR-005), not 403:
  c8aefe75 2026-08-06 08:50 fix(iad-ci): disable base-backup compression to fix ARMOR InvalidPartSize
  d89f8e32 2026-08-06 23:28 fix(iad-ci): ARMOR multipart upload compatibility for CNPG backups
  ARMOR fc6c1a86 2026-08-06 22:51 fix(multipart): allow a lone or final part to be non-block-aligned
  plus the in-file comment block at cnpg-cluster.yaml:71-99 and notes/bf-1zh.md
Different failure mode, different fix. Not a shared cause.

No changes applied (read-only research, as scoped).

issue.description:
## Binding Window Selection and Safe Worker Count

Implement binding window detection across all three windows and safe worker computation.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add binding window and safe worker logic

### What to Implement
- `pub fn find_binding_window(forecasts: &mut [WindowRecord])`:
  - Find the window with the smallest (most negative) margin_hrs
  - Set `bind = 1` on that window, `bind = 0` on others
  - Compute and set `safe_w` only on the binding window
- `pub fn compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct: f64, hrs_left: f64, p75_rate_per_worker: f64) -> u32`:
  - `safe_w = floor(remaining_pct / (p75_rate_per_worker * hrs_left))`
  - If p75_rate_per_worker is 0 or hrs_left is 0, return u32::MAX (no constraint)
  - Floor to nearest integer (conservative)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot: &UsageSnapshot, fleet_rates: &FleetRates, config: &Config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`:
  - Generate 3 WindowRecords (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - Call find_binding_window on the set
  - Return all 3 records ready for JSONL append

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::binding 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: 5h window with margin_hrs=-2 vs 7d with margin_hrs=5 -> 5h is binding
- Unit test: 7d_sonnet most constrained -> it gets bind=1
- Unit test: safe_w computation — remaining=50, hrs_left=10, p75_rate=1.0 -> safe_w=5
- Unit test: safe_w floor behavior — remaining=50, hrs_left=10, p75_rate=1.1 -> safe_w=4 (floor)
- Unit test: safe_w only populated on the binding window, None on others
- Unit test: compute_window_forecasts returns exactly 3 records

## Task: Dollar Computation and Pricing Engine

Compute dollar-equivalent costs from token counts using configurable per-model pricing.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs` (or new `src/pricing.rs`):
  - `PricingConfig` struct: loaded from governor.yaml pricing section
  - `ModelPricing` struct: `input_per_mtok`, `output_per_mtok`, `cache_write_5m_per_mtok`, `cache_write_1h_per_mtok`, `cache_read_per_mtok`
  - `compute_dollars(usage: &UsageRecord, pricing: &ModelPricing) -> DollarBreakdown`
  - `DollarBreakdown` struct: `input_usd`, `output_usd`, `cache_read_usd`, `cache_write_5m_usd`, `cache_write_1h_usd`, `total_usd`
  - Formula: `tokens * rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000`
  - Load pricing from `governor.yaml` config file (serde_yaml deserialization)
  - Handle unknown models: log warning, fall back to nearest known model pricing

### Files
- `src/collector.rs` or `src/pricing.rs` (new module)
- `src/config.rs` (new — YAML config loading, will be reused across phases)
- `config/governor.yaml` (reference config with pricing table)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: Sonnet 4.6 pricing — verify each token type against known rates ($3/$15/$3.75/$6/$0.30 per MTok)
- Unit test: Opus 4.6 pricing — verify $5/$25/$6.25/$10/$0.50 rates (NOT legacy $15/$75)
- Unit test: Haiku 4.5 pricing — verify $1/$5/$1.25/$2/$0.10 rates
- Unit test: zero tokens produces zero dollars
- Unit test: unknown model falls back gracefully with warning

### Acceptance Criteria
- Dollar computation matches hand-calculated values for all supported models
- Pricing loaded from governor.yaml at startup
- Unknown models handled without panic
- Total USD is sum of all five components

### Dependencies

issue.description:
burn_rate.rs:1195:

    let safe = (remaining_pct / (mean_rate_per_worker * hours_remaining)).floor() as u64;

This sizes for a worker running CONTINUOUSLY until the window resets. Close to
a reset, hours_remaining is large while remaining_pct is small, so the quotient
drops below 1.0 and floors to 0 — the governor authorises nothing and the
remaining quota expires.

Measured 2026-09-07 (verified against ccdash: 7d 62% used, fable 76% used, so
the poller is CORRECT and this is not a data problem):

    mean_rate_per_worker = 1.5   (config::default_baseline_pct, uncalibrated)
    hours_remaining      = 29.67 (weekly resets Tue 21:00)
    denominator          = 44.5

    remaining_pct weekly_scoped 14%  -> 0.31 -> 0
    remaining_pct seven_day     28%  -> 0.63 -> 0
    hard_limit_remaining 7d     38%  -> 0.85 -> 0

So with ~30h to reset the governor requires >=44.5% headroom before it will
allow a SINGLE worker. Below that it allows zero, and 38% of a weekly
allowance is discarded.

This inverts the stated purpose. CLAUDE.md section 5: the pool exists to fill
"spare use-or-lose capacity within the 5-hour / 7-day windows". For use-or-lose
quota, exhausting AT the reset boundary is optimal; the formula instead treats
"would exhaust before reset" as failure and conserves a balance that is about
to be destroyed.

Three compounding factors:

1. `.floor()` with no duty-cycling. A result of 0.85 means "one worker for 85%
   of the remaining window" — 25 of the 30 hours — which is both safe and very
   nearly optimal. It becomes 0 instead. There is no notion of running a worker
   for part of the window.

2. It uses `remaining_pct` (target_ceiling - utilization = 90 - 76 = 14) rather
   than `hard_limit_remaining_pct` (100 - utilization = 24). Reserving 10 points
   is defensible against a platform cutoff, but applying it to a use-or-lose
   balance near reset compounds the waste.

3. `mean_rate_per_worker` is the uncalibrated 1.5 baseline because samples = 0,
   and samples only accrue while workers run. Zero workers -> zero samples ->
   the baseline never improves. A cold-start deadlock that only breaks when a
   reset happens to leave >=44.5% headroom. Measured actual burn for one busy
   Opus session this afternoon was ~1%/hr (7d moved 61->62 in about an hour),
   so 1.5 is also pessimistic.

Directions:
  - Size against time-to-reset as a BUDGET to spend, not a rate to sustain:
    allow workers while projected consumption by reset <= remaining headroom.
  - Replace floor() with a duty cycle, or round up when the shortfall is only
    in duration (0.85 workers = 1 worker for 85% of the window).
  - Use hard_limit_remaining_pct when the window is close to reset, keeping the
    ceiling for windows with time left to protect.
  - Seed the baseline from observed session burn rather than a constant, so a
    cold start has a real number.

Verification: with 38% headroom and 29.67h remaining the governor must
authorise >=1 worker, and must still authorise 0 when the projected spend
would cross the hard limit before reset.

issue.description:
Plan spec (Phase 6, CLI Output Layer): 'Color coding: green = OK, yellow = approaching ceiling, red = cutoff risk. Falls back to plain ASCII when NO_COLOR is set or stdout is not a TTY.'

Current implementation (src/status_display.rs): no color codes present. Output is plain text only.

Implementation:
1. Add color helper that checks NO_COLOR env var and is_terminal() before emitting ANSI codes
2. In format_status_dashboard: color window risk column green (OK), yellow (margin < 50% of hrs_left), red (cutoff_risk=true)
3. Color 'BINDING' indicator prominently (bold red or bold yellow)
4. SAFE MODE warning line: bold yellow/red
5. Respect NO_COLOR=1 env var (standard: https://no-color.org/) — strip all ANSI when set
6. Strip ANSI when stdout is not a terminal (non-TTY already handled for JSON mode, but color should also be stripped for piped plain-text output)

No new crate needed — can use raw ANSI escape sequences: \x1b[32m (green), \x1b[33m (yellow), \x1b[31m (red), \x1b[0m (reset), \x1b[1m (bold).
issue.title: Add ANSI color coding to cgov status output with NO_COLOR fallback

issue.description:
## Goal
Fire an alert when the fleet's cache-read-to-total-token ratio stays below a configurable threshold for N consecutive polling intervals. This detects workloads that are not benefiting from prompt caching.

## Why
Low cache efficiency means workers are burning more tokens per task than expected. This affects burn rate accuracy and cost. A sustained drop (not just a single spike) indicates a structural issue worth surfacing.

## Implementation
- In alerts.rs: add LowCacheEfficiency alert variant (already has stub per recent commits)
- Track cache_efficiency_ratio per interval in governor state: cache_reads / total_tokens
- If ratio < config.alerts.low_cache_efficiency_threshold (default: 0.3) for >= N consecutive intervals (default: 3): fire alert
- Alert body: current ratio, threshold, consecutive intervals below threshold
- Respect existing per-alert-type cooldown mechanism
- Expose cache_efficiency_ratio in cgov status output
- Add unit tests for threshold boundary, cooldown, recovery

## Config additions (governor.yaml)
alerts:
  low_cache_efficiency_threshold: 0.3
  low_cache_efficiency_consecutive_intervals: 3

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cache_efficiency_ratio tracked per poll interval
- [ ] Alert fires when ratio sustained below threshold
- [ ] Cooldown respected (no spam)
- [ ] Ratio visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests for boundary conditions
issue.title: Add sustained low cache efficiency alert with configurable threshold and window

issue.description:
scripts/polish-seeder.sh targets bead-forge (`bf`) throughout. bf is not on PATH
on codinghome and every one of the 62 candidate repos is bead-rs (0 repos still
carry .beads/config.yaml). Two independent failures result:

1. UNBOUNDED SEEDING. ready_count() is

       ( cd "$1" && "$BF" ready 2>/dev/null | grep -c "bf-" ) || echo 0

   With bf absent this yields 0 for every repo, so gate (b) "target backlog is
   below LOW_WATER" is always true. The seeder would create a meta-bead for
   every target on every pass. The two-tank property the design depends on —
   generation follows consumption, so it converges — is silently gone. It also
   greps for `bf-` ids, which no bead-rs workspace emits, so even with bf
   installed the count would be 0 against these repos.

2. GENERATOR PROMPTS THAT CANNOT RUN. The meta-bead description instructs the
   strand to run `bf ready`, `bf list`, `bf create ...` in the TARGET repo and
   `bf batch --json ...` in the queue. Those commands do not exist here, so a
   strand burns a full Opus turn, creates nothing, and cannot close its own
   meta-bead — which leaves it pending and blocks re-seeding for that repo.
   Worse if bf is ever reinstalled: per the org CLAUDE.md, running bf against a
   bead-rs store does not fail cleanly, it silently corrupts the schema. This
   would point that at up to 62 repos at once.

Also stale for the same reason: the queue bootstrap hint "run: cd $QUEUE && bf
init" (section 4 of CLAUDE.md was corrected separately in a690e3d).

Fix: port the script to `bead`.
  - ready_count: `bead list --ready` counting `^ID:` lines (verified working
    across all 62 candidate repos).
  - pending meta-bead detection: bead-rs `list --json` is a JSON document, not
    the NDJSON `bf list --json` emitted, so the parser needs replacing too.
  - generator prompt: `bead create --issue-type task --priority 2 --title ...
    --description ...` in the target, and `bead close <ID> --reason ...` in the
    queue (bead-rs has no `batch` verb of the shape used, and close requires a
    reason).
  - drop the BF env var for BEAD, defaulting to `bead` on PATH.

Verification: a dry pass against a repo with a known backlog above LOW_WATER
must skip it, and one below must seed exactly one meta-bead; running the emitted
prompt text by hand must produce beads in the target and close the meta-bead.
issue.title: polish-seeder.sh is written against bf, which is not installed — seeds unboundedly and emits prompts that cannot run

claude-governor.service on codinghome is stopped AND disabled:

  systemctl --user is-active   claude-governor.service  -> inactive
  systemctl --user is-enabled  claude-governor.service  -> disabled

  Sep 13 07:19:38 codinghome systemd[2765]: Stopping Claude Governor ...
  Sep 13 07:19:39 codinghome cgov[619116]: [governor] daemon stopped
  Sep 13 07:19:39 codinghome systemd[2765]: claude-governor.service: Consumed
    25.173s CPU over 2h 45min wall clock, 770.1M memory peak

It was a clean stop, not a crash, so this may have been deliberate — the
adjacent backups (cgov.bak-pre-collectorfix-20260907T124625Z,
claude-governor.service.bak-pre-oomfix-20260907T123609Z) suggest recent
memory/collector work. What was not decided deliberately is the downstream
effect.

DOWNSTREAM BREAKAGE: /home/coding/.config/claude-governor/governor-state.json
was last written 2026-09-13 07:15:25 and is the input to the fleet's GLM
five-hour quota control loop. That consumer now fails every start:

  needle-glm-quota-controller.service: Result=exit-code ExecMainStatus=1
    needle-glm-quota-controller: five-hour quota sample is stale (53563s old)

So GLM quota control for a 27-worker fleet has been blind for ~15 hours, while
21 GLM workers keep dispatching. The last time quota/concurrency control
misbehaved on this host the whole GLM fleet sat idle for 2.5 hours
(NEEDLE needle-e0926811).

WANTED — decide which, then do it:
- If the governor should be running: re-enable and start it, confirm
  governor-state.json advances, confirm needle-glm-quota-controller goes active.
- If it is deliberately retired: say so here, and retire or repoint its
  consumers. A stale state file that a live control loop still trusts is the
  worst of the three options.

Either way, the consumer should degrade rather than exit 1 on stale input —
tracked separately as NEEDLE needle-79044e14.
issue.notes:
Outcome recorded by claudego-45001e32 (the consumer-side alternative): IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED. Commit 030ac19 in claude-governor vendors the controller as scripts/needle-glm-quota-controller (deployed copy at /home/coding/bin is byte-identical). On stale/missing/unusable governor-state.json the controller now self-samples via `cgov poll --format json` (60s timeout, read-only usage poll on the on-disk OAuth creds, no daemon needed), backfills the fresh sample into governor-state.json under cgov's state lock, and only when the self-sample ALSO fails degrades to action=stale-hold-conservative with exit 0 (keeps LOCAL_BASE up, sheds <=1 lab unit/pass, records sample age). Exit 1 is reserved for the controller's own local failures.

Current live posture on codinghome (2026-09-17T18:08Z): claude-governor.service is still inactive, but claude-governor-observe.service (added by 1b2b54b) is active and governor-state.json is fresh (updated_at 18:07:59Z, five_hour_pct 3.0), so the original stale-input condition does not currently reproduce; needle-glm-quota-controller.service is inactive, not failing. The deliberate-retirement-vs-re-enable decision this bead asks for remains the operator's; the downstream breakage is fixed either way.

Update 2026-09-17 (claudego-e16a7eb1, the conservative-posture alternative): the posture is verified end to end and hardened - commit aeb9d91 in claude-governor closes two residual exit-1 holes (a fresh sample with no usage subtree used to raise KeyError out of main; a null last_scale_at in the controller's own state) and pins all five degrade behaviors in tests/glm_quota_controller_stale_hold.rs (stale hold with masked-unit handling and exactly one unmasked shed, MIN_SCALE_INTERVAL_SECS blocking the shed, missing file -> null age, malformed usage -> degrade not exit 1, unwritable own state -> exit 1). Verification ran fully sandboxed via the script's documented env overrides plus PATH shims for systemctl/ssh/journalctl/cgov - the live fleet and live state files were never touched.

## Task: Decision Narration and Audit Log (cgov explain)

Make every scaling decision transparent with plain-English explanations and a persistent audit log.

### What to Implement
- New `src/narrator.rs` module:
  - Template-based text generator (no LLM — pure string formatting)
  - `narrate_decision(before: &GovernorState, after: &GovernorState, action: &ScaleAction) -> DecisionEntry`
  - `DecisionEntry`: ts, action, from, to, reason (human-readable), trigger, binding_window, margin_before, margin_after
  - Templates for each action type: scale_up, scale_down, sprint_activate, sprint_deactivate, pre_scale, emergency_brake_engage, emergency_brake_release, promotion_transition, cutoff_risk_transition (safe->risk, risk->safe), prediction_accuracy_score
  - Append to `~/.needle/state/governor-decisions.jsonl`
  - `cgov explain` subcommand:
    - Default: show latest decision with formatted explanation
    - `--last N`: show N most recent decisions
    - `--json`: emit raw JSONL records
  - Narration includes specific numbers (window name, percentages, hours, worker counts)

### Files
- `src/narrator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov explain` subcommand)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: narrate scale_up with expected explanation text
- Unit test: narrate scale_down with specific numbers
- Unit test: narrate sprint activation
- Unit test: narrate emergency brake
- Unit test: narrate cutoff risk transition

### Acceptance Criteria
- Every scaling action generates a decision entry
- Human-readable explanations with specific data points
- JSONL audit log is append-only
- cgov explain provides both human and JSON output
- Templates cover all action types from plan

### Dependencies

## Incremental JSONL Reader with Shrinkage Guard

Implement the incremental line reader that seeks to a byte offset and reads new lines, with shrinkage detection for log-rotated files.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add incremental reader function

### What to Implement
- `pub fn read_new_lines(path: &Path, cursor: &mut CursorStore) -> Result<Vec<String>>`:
  - Get stored offset via cursor.get_offset(path)
  - Check current file size: if file size < stored offset, log warning `[collector] cursor reset for {path} (file shrunk: {stored} -> {actual} bytes)` and reset offset to 0
  - Seek to byte offset, read all bytes to EOF
  - Split into lines, filter out empty lines
  - Update cursor with new byte offset (end of file)
  - Return the new lines as Vec<String>

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::read_new 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: write 3 lines to temp file, read_new_lines with offset 0 returns all 3 lines
- Unit test: incremental read — write 2 lines, read (get 2), write 2 more, read again (get only new 2), verify cursor offset updated
- Unit test: shrinkage guard — write 100 bytes, set cursor offset to 100, truncate file to 10 bytes, read_new_lines resets offset to 0 and returns all content
- Unit test: empty file returns empty Vec
- Unit test: file with trailing newline doesn't produce empty trailing line
- Shrinkage guard must log the warning message (capture log output or use tracing test subscriber)
issue.title: Incremental JSONL reader with shrinkage guard

issue.description:
cgov cannot scale a pool up from zero workers. Every path that produces a
per-worker burn rate requires workers to already be running, so a fleet at 0
stays at 0 regardless of available headroom.

The chain, in burn_rate.rs::estimate_burn_rates:

  1. let mut p75_per_worker = if current_workers > 0 {
         stats.p75_pct_hr / current_workers as f64
     } else {
         0.0                      // <-- zero workers => zero rate
     };

  2. The cold-start seeding that exists precisely to supply a rate when there is
     no calibration is ALSO gated on workers already running:

         if is_cold_start && util > 0.0 && current_workers > 0 {
             fleet_pct_hr   = base_per_worker * current_workers as f64;
             p75_per_worker = base_per_worker;
         }

  3. p75_per_worker is what is passed as `mean_rate_per_worker` into
     generate_window_forecast, and both the old floor path and the new
     duty_cycle_safe_workers bail on a non-positive rate:

         if !(per_worker_rate > 0.0) || ... { return 0; }

So: 0 workers -> rate 0 -> authorised 0 -> 0 workers. A closed loop.

IMPORTANT: this survives the duty-cycle fix. duty_cycle_safe_workers correctly
authorises one worker for any positive budget, but it never sees a positive
budget from a standing start, because per_worker_rate is 0. Landing that fix
alone will change nothing observable, which is a bad failure mode -- it will
look like the fix did not work.

Also note is_cold_start = !has_fresh_rate && samples < MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA.
`has_fresh_rate` is true whenever ANY instance record exists for the window this
interval -- including records from an operator's own interactive Claude Code
session, which have nothing to do with the fleet. So an idle fleet plus an
active operator session is not even classified as cold-start, and the seeding
branch is skipped for that reason too. See claudego-0ccbae3c.

FIX OPTIONS:

  a. Let the cold-start branch seed at current_workers == 0, using the
     configured baseline as a HYPOTHETICAL per-worker rate: the question being
     asked is "if I ran one worker, could I afford it?", which does not require
     a worker to exist. Drop `&& current_workers > 0` from the seeding
     condition and seed p75_per_worker = base_per_worker (leaving fleet_pct_hr
     at its measured value, which is correct -- it is what is actually burning).

  b. Fall back to baseline.pct_per_worker_per_hour whenever
     p75_per_worker == 0.0, at the point of use rather than in the seeding
     branch.

  c. Operationally, seed by hand: launch one worker whose session name matches
     a configured pool's session_pattern, so current_workers becomes 1 and the
     normal calibration path engages. This unblocks a single instance but is
     not a fix -- the pool cannot recover on its own after ever reaching 0,
     which is the state cgov deliberately scales pools down to.

(c) is worth recording because it means the scale-to-0 behaviour is one-way:
any pool cgov scales to zero can never be restarted by cgov.

Verification: with zero workers running, a configured pool, and real headroom
in the binding window, cgov must authorise >= 1 worker and launch it. Cover it
with a test that asserts a non-zero authorised count for current_workers == 0.

issue.description:
Presentation defect only — the scaling logic is correct and must not be changed
for this (see claudego-b9e2f08e, whose factor 2 was withdrawn for exactly this
reason).

`cgov status` emits per window:

    used_pct    = 62.0
    remain_pct  = 28.0
    ceiling_pct = 90.0

used_pct + remain_pct = 90, not 100. remain_pct is headroom below the 90%
TARGET CONSUMPTION ceiling, which is a deliberate and correct thing to budget
against. But published under the name "remain_pct" directly alongside
"used_pct", it reads as remaining quota, and a reader concludes the account has
28% left when it actually has 38% before the platform cutoff.

`hard_limit_remaining_pct` (100 - utilization = 38.0) already exists on
WindowForecast with a doc comment stating precisely this distinction — it is
simply never exported. The published field list is: binding, ceiling_pct,
cone_ratio, cutoff_risk, exh_hrs_p25/p50/p75, remain_pct, resets_in_hrs, risk,
risk_score, used_pct.

This actively misled a live capacity decision on 2026-09-07: the operator read
62% used in ccdash and knew 38% was left, while cgov reported "remain 28%", and
reconciling the two took a code read. ceiling_pct is present so the gap is
derivable, but nothing states it.

Fix (status_display.rs:548 and the human-readable renderer):
  - export hard_limit_remaining_pct alongside remain_pct, and
  - rename the exported key to something that says what it is, e.g.
    remain_to_ceiling_pct, keeping remain_pct as a deprecated alias for one
    release so existing consumers do not break.

Verification: for a window at 62% used with a 90% ceiling, the output must
contain both 28 (to ceiling) and 38 (to hard limit), each under a name that
distinguishes them.
issue.notes: Verified already shipped in HEAD (commit 6e60abe, which landed alongside the claudego-d64682d5 pool-sizing fix). All three required changes are present in src/status_display.rs: (1) JSON exports hard_limit_remaining_pct; (2) key renamed remain_pct -> remain_to_ceiling_pct with remain_pct kept as deprecated alias; (3) human renderer has separate Remain% and HardLim% columns plus legend 'Remain% = headroom to ceiling; HardLim% = headroom to platform cutoff (100%)'. Tests format_json_distinguishes_ceiling_and_hard_limit_remaining and format_dashboard_labels_ceiling_and_hard_limit_remaining encode exactly the bead's verification scenario (62 used / 90 ceiling -> 28 and 38) and pass: 2 passed, 0 failed. No scaling logic touched. End-to-end on the deployed binary (built 2026-09-12, newer than the fix commit): status --json shows seven_day used_pct 62.0, remain_to_ceiling_pct 23.0 (ceiling 85), hard_limit_remaining_pct 38.0, remain_pct 23.0 alias intact; pty-rendered dashboard shows both columns and legend. HEAD == origin/main, so the fix is pushed. No file changes needed from this dispatch; the pre-dirty working-tree files belong to other in-flight beads and were left untouched.
